case_name: Sree Vijayakumar and Anr v State, By Inspector of Police, Kanyakumari
respondent:
State, By Inspector of Police, Kanyakumari
Supreme Court of India

13  May  2005
Appeal (crl.) 627 of 2004
The Judgment was delivered by : P. Venkatarama Reddi, J.
1. Accused Nos. 1 & 2 in the Sessions case No. 91 of 1998 (on the file of the Additional Sessions Judge, Kanyakumari) are the appellants in this appeal. They were prosecuted along with two
facts: A dispute arose between the father of the accused and the deceased and his family members in connection with an electricity line passing through the father's house of the accused.

On 21.7.1994, at about 7.30 p.m., when Rajeswaran was going past the shop of the 2nd appellant Rajagopal to purchase some articles from a nearby shop, the 1st appellant Vijaya Kumar came out of the shop and started abusing him and then took out a bottle and hit it on the head of the deceased.
The victim was admitted into the Government hospital, Nagercoil with 90% burn injuries and he died in the hospital on 24.7.1994.
The appellants and two others were also charged for attempting to murder PW1 the brother of the deceased by stabbing him.
A3 & A4 who were the acquitted accused, caught hold of Rajeswaran and did not allow him to move.
At that moment, the 2nd appellant Rajagopal picked up a lighted kerosene lamp from his shop and threw it on Rajeswaran.
issues: The genesis of the incident has been suppressed by the prosecution.
No action was taken to promptly inquire into the counter complaint given by the accused.
The appellants and another accused had received serious injuries which remained unexplained by the prosecution witnesses.
The evidence of the brothers of deceased who were chance witnesses has been deliberately introduced to build up the prosecution case.
petitioner_arguments: The genesis of the incident has been suppressed by the prosecution.
No action was taken to promptly inquire into the counter complaint given by the accused.
The appellants and another accused had received serious injuries which remained unexplained by the prosecution witnesses.
The evidence of the brothers of deceased who were chance witnesses has been deliberately introduced to build up the prosecution case.
respondent_arguments: There is trust-worthy evidence of eye-witnesses apart from the dying declaration recorded by the Magistrate and that there are no grounds to interfere with the concurrent findings of fact.
Petrol was detected on the skin of the deceased and this fact goes to corroborate the prosecution version.
The accused had motive to cause harm to the deceased by reason of previous enimity.
court_reasoning: The appellants totally denied the incident and their involvement.
The investigation even in regard to Cr. No.377/94 giving rise to the present case went on for three years and 4 or 5.

The First Information Report based on the alleged statement made by the deceased to Head Constable (PW12) is not acceptable as PW12 admitted that FIR was prepared after consultation with the superior officers and that the contents of the statement were not made known to the witnesses who signed it.
holding: Appellants 1 & 2 were convicted for the offence under Section 302 with the aid of Section 34 IPC and the sentence of life imprisonment was confirmed.
Their conviction and sentence under Section 324 read with Section 34 was also confirmed.
